sources.title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT 14.381 — Lecture 2: Limit Theorems (Fall 2018)
sources.retrieval: Actual six-page PDF retrieved and all substantive printed pages 1–5 read; pages 4–5 also rendered locally and visually inspected. Official course identifies instructor and Fall 2018.
sources.scope: Finite-variance LLN, scalar/vector CLT statements, probability versus distribution convergence, stochastic orders, Slutsky and first-order delta reasoning. Original chapter proofs/examples must state their own assumptions.
sources.source_cautions: Printed page 4 omits an absolute value in the Op tail definition and omits centering in its sample-mean order example; do not adopt those literal formulas. The source mean-value proof assumes continuous derivative. Use a norm-based stochastic bound and a differentiability remainder proof. General dependence and Lindeberg-Feller extensions are not established by the new chapter merely by citing these notes.

sources.title: Victor Chernozhukov, MIT 14.385 — Lecture 2: Consistency for Extremum Estimators (Fall 2007)
sources.retrieval: Actual 23-page PDF retrieved. Read physical pages 10–19 covering compact extremum consistency, proof, identification warning, measurability, pointwise/uniform distinction, ULLN and finite-grid idea. Physical pages 10 and 12 rendered and visually inspected.
sources.scope: Separation plus uniform criterion convergence as sufficient conditions for consistency. Chapter will independently prove a finite-dimensional compact approximate-minimizer result and a bounded/Lipschitz finite-net ULLN.
sources.source_cautions: No claim to reproduce or verify all mixing-process, outer-probability, convexity or nonlinear-choice extensions. State measurability/separability explicitly; pointwise consistency across laws is distinct from uniform-in-parameter criterion convergence.

sources.title: Peter Kempthorne, MIT 18.655 — Lecture 16: Asymptotics, Consistency and Delta Method (Spring 2016)
sources.retrieval: Actual 33-page PDF retrieved; read slides 3–11 on consistency/plug-ins and slides 22–23 on distributional delta/studentization. Slide 22 rendered and visually inspected.
sources.scope: Consistent plug-in functionals, first-order differentiability remainder and studentized mean. Original exact examples will distinguish weak distributional limits from convergence of moments.
sources.source_cautions: Do not adopt uncentered shorthand in the sample-mean bound or claim finite-sample coverage from a limit theorem. No source examples, images or numerical problems reproduced.

sources.title: David Aldous, Probability Theory (Berkeley C205B/C218B, Spring 2017), notes by Sinho Chewi — Lecture 8, Cramér–Wold device
sources.retrieval: Actual104-page instructor-hosted PDF retrieved. Read title and printed31–33 (physical32–34): Theorems8.1,8.2,8.4 and Gaussian covariance construction. Printed31/physical32 rendered locally and visually inspected.
sources.scope: Direct support for the explicitly invoked finite-dimensional Cramér–Wold characterization; scalar projections identify a joint limit when a matching vector law exists. The chapter derives its scalar-contrast limits and constructs the Gaussian candidate from a covariance square root.
sources.source_cautions: The source reduces the device to a multivariate characteristic-function continuity theorem which is invoked there. This does not amount to a full foundational proof in this chapter. The printed32 tightness display has an n-versus-k sum-index slip; use trace covariance independently. No later Markov/ergodic material read or certified.

design_boundaries: All original proofs and examples; accepted Volume 2/3/4 methods supply prior tools. Three worked examples and at least ten fully solved graduate exercises, including proofs and research critique.
Identify target and observable law before estimator. Give a two-world nonidentification construction, identified-set and model-dependent target distinctions.

Develop probability/distribution convergence and stochastic orders with quantifiers and exact rare-event counterexamples. Prove compact approximate extremum consistency and one sufficient uniform LLN by finite net.

Derive asymptotically linear expansion, studentization and multivariate delta with valid covariance. Provide zero-derivative/nonregular counterexample; do not infer moment convergence or universal uniform coverage.
No extra framework, random-grid artifact or installations. Any reproducible demonstration must be focused and exact or numerically documented, with standard-library code only.
limitations: Source preparation is not a completed chapter; manuscripts, full independent proof/solution checks, separate peer, canonical integration and publishing remain. Locally rendered source PDF pages do not satisfy pending textbook reader UI QA.
